title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'deuxième mouture' of Analysis situs (June 1986), Grothendieck is axiomatizing an 'atelier'. This is a tame-topological framework with a set 𝔉 of 'figures', a subset 𝓜 ⊂ 𝔉 of strata (irreducible pieces), and a set 𝓛 of minimal figures (defined on the next page via ≪). On the previous page he had just introduced the incidence relation F ⊲ G :⟺ F ≤ G and F ∈ 𝓜 ('F is a stratum of G'), noting that it gives a geometric characterization.

This page does three things.

(1.18) Diagram of the six fundamental relations on 𝔉 and the implications between them:
- G⊲F ⇒ G≤F;
- G≤F ⇒ G≪F and G≤F ⇒ G≬F;
- G≼F ⇒ G≪F;
- G∥F ⇒ G≬F.
A box encloses G≤F and G≪F. Plausibly ≤ is the basic order on figures, ≪ is a coarser 'refinement' order, and ≼ is a stricter refinement. ∥ is disjointness, since F∥F ⟺ F = ∅. ≬ is a symmetric, reflexive 'compatibility / position-compatible' relation; by (1.27) on the next page, G ≤ F ⟺ G ≪ F and G ≬ F.

Classification: ⊲, ≤, ≼, ≪ are called order relations; ∥ and ≬ are symmetric. ≬ is reflexive, while ∥ is reflexive only on the empty figure (1.19), so it is reflexive only when 𝔉 = {∅_𝔉}. The margin note corrects this: ⊲ is not an order in the strict (reflexive) sense, since F⊲F ⟺ F ∈ 𝓜. It is a genuine partial order only on 𝓜.

Remark a) ≤ and ⊲ determine each other.
- From ≤ to ⊲: 𝓜 is the set of 'strictly irreducible' elements, X ≤ sup_i F_i ⇒ ∃i, X ≤ F_i (completely join-prime elements); then ⊲ is given by (1.17).
- From ⊲ to ≤: 𝓜 = {X | X⊲X}. The 'déploiement' is F̃ = {X ∈ 𝓜 | X⊲F}, and F ≤ G ⟺ F̃ ⊂ G̃.

In modern terms this is the Birkhoff–Raney representation. A complete lattice in which every element is the join of the completely join-prime elements below it is isomorphic, via F ↦ F̃, to the lattice of down-sets of the poset (𝓜, ≤). The atelier is then an Alexandrov-type structure on the poset of strata, like the face poset of a stratification. The conclusion, continued on p.12, is that one may take either ≤ or ⊲ as the basic datum. The next page goes on to show that ≤ or ≪ determines ∥, that ≪ determines ≼ and 𝓛, and that ≪ together with ≬ recovers ≤.
errors: Calling ⊲ an 'order relation' is inaccurate on 𝔉, since it is not reflexive outside 𝓜; the margin note itself flags this. It is a partial order only on 𝓜 (or a 'strict-type' relation on 𝔉).

The converse claim (1.23), F ≤ G ⟺ F̃ ⊂ G̃, needs the axiom that every figure is the sup of the strata it contains (join-density of 𝓜). That axiom is presumably among the atelier axioms but is not stated here.
That ∅ ∉ 𝓜 follows correctly from (1.20) only if empty families are allowed (sup ∅ = ∅_𝔉). This is implicit.

ideas.what: Diagram of implications among six relations on figures: incidence, inclusion, two refinement orders, disjointness, compatibility
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatics of stratified / tame spaces via relations on the poset of definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal / tame topology (van den Dries, Shiota) for the setting; no standard analogue of this relational presentation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 only announces 'topologie modérée' programmatically

ideas.what: Recovering the lattice of figures from the incidence relation on strata via the 'déploiement' F̃, and conversely the strata as strictly (completely) join-irreducible elements
ideas.modern_name: Birkhoff / Raney representation of completely distributive lattices by down-sets of completely join-prime elements; Alexandrov topology on the face poset

ideas.what: Disjointness relation characterized by F∥F ⟺ F empty; compatibility relation reflexive and symmetric

missed.claim: Grothendieck's relational axiomatics of 'ateliers' is unpublished and not taken up in the literature. It axiomatizes tame topology through figures, strata, incidence and refinement relations, and asks which relations suffice to determine the structure (≤ ⟺ ⊲; ≪ + ≬ ⟹ ≤). Comparable 'minimal data' questions for o-minimal or stratified categories are not treated in this form.
missed.quote: Les relations ⊲ et ≤ se déterminent mutuellement
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a combinatorial/order-theoretic foundation for tame topology and for stratified homotopy theory (posets of strata, exit paths), complementary to o-minimality. The page itself is mostly routine lattice theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of the little-known atelier axiomatics, but the mathematics on this page is standard order theory (Birkhoff representation) plus bookkeeping of relations.
transcription_corrections: 'Remarques 1)' should read 'Remarques a)', since the next page continues with b), c), d), e).
The equation label is (1.18), and the arrows read: ⊲⇒≤; ≤⇒≪ and ≤⇒≬; ≼⇒≪ (crossing arrow); ∥⇒≬.
'symétriques. {+de plus,+} La relation ≬ est réflexive' should read 'symétriques. De plus, la relation ≬ est réflexive'.
The margin note is roughly: 'Noter ⊲ n'est pas une rel. d'ordre au sens ordinaire (pas réflexive) ; 𝓜 est l'ens. des F tels que F⊲F ...'. Its formulas F⊲F are partly illegible.

In the last line, 'fixant la structure de treillis [?]' is more likely 'fixant la structure d'atelier', and the sentence continues on p.12 with '...d'y prendre comme données principales soit ≤, soit ⊲'.
